utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us resume our work for a long afternoon. Let me say hello to the interpreters. (Translation feed difficulties)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Now I'm getting English, Mr. President. I was getting BCS, so perhaps it's sorted out now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You know that the French is always a martyr language, but everything has been restored to order, I hope. In that case, we can resume our work. According to the registry, the public gallery is not receiving transmissions. For the moment, we do not have video transmissions in the public gallery. It will be delayed. Can the public gallery hear us now when we're speaking? Normally, they should be able to. Let us resume work. Let me remind you that the examination-in-chief of the witness, Brigadier Ivica Zeko -- Ivica Zeko; is that right? Ivica Zeko. Mr. Nobilo, we can continue. I think that you were in charge of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. Could I ask the usher to bring in Brigadier Zeko? (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No translation. Channel six?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. We're going to resume our work. May I remind you that on the 11th of September, you were questioned by counsel for the accused who called you to testify in the trial -- there seems to be a technical problem. I'm getting the English interpretation. Let me continue. Has it been corrected? Is it all right now? Yes. Let us continue with the examination-in-chief of the Brigadier. I wish to remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we continue with the examination-in-chief, in reviewing the transcript, we noted a number of imprecisions or, rather, two to them, which probably occurred either due to the interpretation or to the transcript. The first mistake is on page 11677 in the first paragraph, and to eliminate any dilemmas, let me ask a question. It appears from this that part of the 7th Muslim and 17th Krajina Brigades were in Gacice and Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question is: Were parts of these units in Stari Vitez and Gacice, or did those units direct their activities towards those villages and those localities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, these units were acting in the direction of those villages. They were not in Stari Vitez or Gacice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Another error of the same kind on the next page, 11668, also at the beginning, it says that the 306th Brigade was within the zone of the village of Grbavica, and it tried to break communications between Vitez and Busovaca and Vitez and Nova Bila; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. The 306th Brigade was directed along that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, when you were listing all the brigades, you drew my attention, after last week's testimony, that all the brigades of the 3rd Corps had not been drawn in, that there had been an error made where the maps were drawn. Would you please tell us which brigades of the 3rd Corps on the table that you presented here, a copy of which has been handed to the Prosecution, which brigades have been left out?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the diagram showing the structure of the 3rd Corps has omitted to mention two brigades from Visoko, the 315th and the 316th Mountain Brigade, also the 370th Brigade from Donji Vakuf, and the 311th Brigade from Kakanj. And also in the command of the 3rd Corps, there was an additional unit, a company for electronic activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue with your presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we have the monitor switched on, please, and the lights dimmed slightly? Mr. Dubuisson, can the lights be dimmed, please? Thank you. Can the monitor also be switched on so we can look at this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please, in your own words, describe this, but let us just go back for a moment to recall the range of artillery of the Serbian forces and the BH army forces?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this map shows in red the units of the army of Republika Srpska, then also, the zone of operations of artillery weapons from the region of Rakovica, the village of Potkraj, using 122 millimetre weapons and 122 mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, does this mean that Serbs from Rakovica could shell Kiseljak and Visoko?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to Mount Vlasic. What were the positions of the artillery and what was their range?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On Mount Vlasic, the Vlasic Plateau, the position of the Hamajndzic (phoen) Platoon, artillery pieces of 155 millimetre calibre were positioned there. The region of Majokrnja (phoen) next to the village of Bijelo Bucje, 155 millimetre howitzers and 130 millimetre guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The 155 millimetre howitzers and 130 millimetre guns that the Serbs had on Mount Vlasic, do they cover the town of Zenica in terms of the range of those artillery weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In yellow, we see the communications within the Lasva River Valley, which was the key supply route for both units and the population in the Lasva Valley. Most of the battles were fought over this route.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, from Croatia and from Herzegovina, was it possible to reach the Lasva Valley without passing along this road?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The blue indicates the special purpose production in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "special purpose production"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I mean the military industry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you describe where the military factories were and what they manufactured and who controlled each of those military factories?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The Slobodan Princep Seljo factory in Bugojno produced anti-tank and anti-infantry mines, all kinds of fuses for mines, and hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who had control of that factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was controlled by the BH army. Next, the factory Bratsvo in Novi Travnik manufactured all types of artillery pieces from 60 to 152 millimetre calibre, launchers of 128 millimetre calibre, and the Oganj and Vatra (phoen) systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Those are rocket systems?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who controlled that factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was also under the control of the BH army. Then the Technical and Maintenance Institute at Travnik mainly dealt with signals devices for this area, that is, where devices for control and command over a brigade were assembled. And those devices or, rather, vehicles, they happened to be in that institute, that is, there were more than 20 of such communications vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who controlled that factory which produced vehicles for communication centres?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They were command vehicles, and the factory was under the control of the BH army, and they had full control over those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the HVO receive a single of those vehicles with all the communications equipment inside? What about Bratsvo, Novi Travnik, who controlled it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The BH army controlled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: One of your answers is missing from the transcript, so allow me to repeat the question, and will you please repeat the answer? My question is: Did the HVO receive a single vehicle which represented a command and communications centre for a brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us proceed. Which was the next military factory in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The next one is the Slobodan Princep Seljo factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did that factory manufacture?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It manufactured military explosives.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it the only one in this part of Europe?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, at the time, the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Under whose control was it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The next factory for the military industry was in the Zenica Ironworks which manufactured castings for shells and charges for all calibre shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of course, the BH army controlled that in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The next factory is the IGM in Konjic, a factory of ammunition which manufactured ammunition from 7.62 millimetres to 12.7 millimetre calibre and shells for anti-air defences and anti-air guns, that is, guns of 20 and 40 millimetre calibres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me now, these factories obviously form a military industrial chain of the former Yugoslavia, most of which was concentrated in Central Bosnia. Is it possible to establish production of artillery and everything artillery needs without gaining control of the Slobodan Princep Seljo factory of explosives in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, the BH army had the whole chain of production, with the exception of the explosives factory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us continue with the zones of responsibility within the territory of Central Bosnia, and who had control of this key supply route?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Indicated in green are the zones of responsibility of the BH army. The zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps was inclusive of Gornji Vakuf and including Visoko. The 2nd Corps did not exclude Visoko, and its zone of responsibility was in the direction of Tuzla. The 1st Corps did not include Visoko, and parts of its brigade covered Vares and Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have now indicated the zones of responsibility of various operative groups and corps that can be seen from the map, but let us hear what your conclusion is. Was it possible to use the key supply route without passing through zones under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us please continue with the Mujahedin units. Where were they and what did they signify in this area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: These green circles stand for Mujahedin camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your understanding, or the understanding of the people in the Lasva Valley, what does the word "Mujahedin" mean? How would you describe them? What significance did you attach to them and what was the purpose of their coming to the area?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, Mujahedin is the word that they themselves used. That is what they call themselves and their appearance was such that they wore unusual garb. They wore a beard and their clothing in general differed from the others. It was not typical of the clothing worn by a soldier that we would come across in the area. Also, the Islamic rights included a prohibition on the use of alcohol. Also, there were instructions given to Muslim combatants containing -- I may say that they -- the texts were frightening, especially for the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The local Muslims who had lived with you for centuries, how did they react to these Mujahedins from foreign countries?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They too were afraid of them and they were not glad to see them in the neighbouring villages and other localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so this error in the transcript doesn't go uncorrected, the witness said "these texts were frightening," t-e-x-t-s, and it was transcribed as the attacks were frightening. He was referring to the written instructions given to members of these units and the word was text not attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like now to ask the registrar to take the document we are going to produce now. These are the basic instructions given to a Muslim combatant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: While these are being prepared and distributed, can you please tell me whether these Mujahedins were blamed by the Croatian people for most of the crimes they had perpetrated against the civilians?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did they introduce new customs, that they would kidnap a young woman and take her from the village and give some money to the father?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, they were taking not women, mostly young women, age 14 to 15.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is D184.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the second paragraph where it says the relation towards the enemy civilians and also point to -- let me read it now to you -- and could you tell us whether you've already seen that document; if so, where and when? So, "the relations towards the enemy civilians, the women and the children, as well as all the other civilians that helped the enemy can be killed and they ought to be treated in the same way as the attackers." And towards the end there is a seal, which is a very specific and characteristic one. Now, Brigadier, tell me, did you see this document during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where and when and how did you get this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I received this document from the citizens of Travnik, who, at that time, received it from a neighbour of theirs, I mean this brochure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the Croatian people in the Central Bosnia know about the deeds of the Mujahedins and about such instructions?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Of this particular document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, apart from the Croatian text we've also got the A version in French and the B version of it, which is the English text translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, I have got it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is D184, 184A for the French translation and D184B for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, where were the Mujahedins? Where were their centres and where did they live?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The Mujahedin camps were near Novi Travnik in the Village of Duboka. It cannot be seen. On the map there is Ravno Rostovo, where they had a training centre. There was also the village of Mehurici. There was one at Podbrezje just at the outskirts of Zenica. Also, in the direction just on the outskirts of Zenica towards Zepce, there is a village of Arnauti. Above Busovaca in the village of Zivcici and above Kiseljak there was the facility and the village Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you know of Mujahedins living in groups, for example, in Sarajevo, or anywhere else outside from the Central Bosnian region?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Those people who, according to your description, which I think corresponds, more or less, to the description of what we can see on the TV when we see the Taliban from Afghanistan. So what inference did it have to the civilians of Central Bosnia where there were half Bosnians, half Croatians?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They were very frightened by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now move on to the following slide and see the routes in Central Bosnia. What was their importance? There were even new roads that were being built -- don't describe it -- but please tell us just symbolically what each colour represents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On this map we can see routes used by the BH army. Those are marked in green. These are the existing routes. And in red there are newly constructed roads used by the BH army. In blue routes used by the HVO and in light blue colour, the newly built roads used by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why did the HVO and the BH army construct new roads, isn't it an unusual situation in the war to build roads?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: All the roads were built only for the units and the supplying of units. The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the newly built one, Travnik, Novi Travnik, used for supplies and also the units used for the units that transferred towards Novi Travnik via Duboko to Kruscica. They were going from Zenica down to the command post in Poculica down to Sivino Selo. And there was another going from Busovaca via to Grbavica. The later road was used for tank units, i.e., to bring tanks to these positions; whereas, the other roads were used for units and supplies because they were unable to use the main communications and that is why new roads were built. The same goes for the light -- the roads marked in light blue which were built by the HVO, also because they were unable to use the main route. The main route being under fire and used by the units of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we move on to summarise and draw conclusions from what you've just told us. What can the conclusion be? What was the centre of activities of the BH army in the period relevant to us going from spring of 1992 -- '93 to February 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The conclusion can be the following: That the BH army managed to cut off and splitting off of the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia to divide it into five enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, in blue, mark the territories under the control of the HVO; green under the BH army and red under the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: We can see that at the very latest in January, 1993, up until the Washington Agreements, BH army was concentrated against the HVO using its 3rd Corps, plus some additional units from the 1st, the 5th Corps and the newly formed 6th Corps, newly formed somewhere during the summer of 1993, somewhere towards the end of July and early August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we're now discussing the slide or the map No. 14. To the best of your knowledge, there were the 3rd Corps plus another 4 corps, so, all in all, some five corps were directed against the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia. Sir, how many men were directed against you in the spring of 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: According to our assessments, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina used some 82 to 84.000 soldiers during that period of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sir, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina used some 82 to 84.000 soldiers during that time period, how many soldiers were at the disposal of the HVO in the same period?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Around 8.200 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Sorry, how many did you say? 8.200 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Between 8.000 to 8.200.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So if we could simplify the proportion, it would be 1 to 10 in favour of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If we see the development of the BH army and its deployment over the territories and you compare it to the front they had towards the Serbs, could you tell us your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The positions and the deployment of the BH army was as follows: First of all, in the areas with mixed populations, then there was a very small front towards the defences of the Bosnian Serbs. And then that deployment showed us what the real objectives of the BH army were. Furthermore, the control of the communications as we could see in the previous slide --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment. You said such deployment should frontline with the Serbs. And also there was the deployment in perhaps in the areas with mixed populations show the real objectives of the army. Could you tell us what these real objectives were?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The real objectives were to take control over the areas where the HVO was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, you told us that there were over 80.000 soldiers of the BH army that were used against the Croats then. That during those two years, the BH army moved its frontlines towards the Serbs for one single metre?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, neither did they undertake any offensive action against the Bosnian Serbs. On the contrary, during that time period, the BH army came into contact with the Bosnian Serb army in the region of Turbe, where they bought and sell weapons and armament as well as food.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before I interrupted you, you were saying that the army wanted to gain control over the key communications in the Lasva River Valley, so it wanted to control territory. Can you now tell us your conclusions, why did they want to gain control over Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, by putting Central Bosnia under their control, they could have all the military manufacturers under their control and have all the production of ammunition and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did they manage to also join their cause in one whole?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina mananged to link up all the corps except for the 5th Corps, meaning the 2nd, the 3rd, the 1st, the 4th and the newly formed 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we now have the following slide which shows the Lasva River Valley after the Washington Agreement, once the peace arrived again in the Lasva River Valley?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: There are green arrows that show the direction of attack of the Bosnian army on the enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on, please. So, this is the territory inside the blue line would represent the territory under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. And what is inside a green line is under the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. What is outside the green line also represents the territory under the control of BH army and what is in red represents the position of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is the position in the moment when the peace was reached?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we now go on to the following document, please. Mr. President, we have got the original version, which is in Croatian. We have also received the English translation, but we would like to excuse us because we did not receive the French translation from the translation unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So it's D184 for the Croatian version and D184A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please correct the transcript because this document is marked D-185.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you please tell us, did you see this document by the Municipal Staff of Municipality of Kiseljak from 1992, the 22nd of May -- the judges have got the text, we're not going to read it. Could you please give us your comments, what did this document mean and what are its contents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It contains the preparation of the unit of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, preparation for the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And, please, could you correct the translation. Upon the answer whether -- upon my question whether the witness had already seen this document, the answer was yes. Could you please tell us, Brigadier Zeco, when did you see it? Was it yesterday or during the war? Or much earlier? What does it mean during the war or after the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: During the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Does this document also give plans for blocking roads?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The problem again is in the transcript. Could you please explain to us what is the plan of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the 5th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: According to the information gathered by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which, at that time, was the Territorial Defence, was to continue collecting information about the HVO, which is already calling aggressors and to commit their units to reinforce action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My colleague has informed me that the transcript does -- is senseless. I'll ask the question once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Who is responsible for the transcript, please? We had the same problem earlier on before we interrupted our hearings, and we see the same thing today. What is going on? I know it is a very delicate type of work, but this is the first time that we are having so many difficulties. This is maybe the first time that we have noted so many problems, because it is usually the parties that do it after the hearings. Well, I'm trying to just reply to the registrar. Normally, all the parties, I think the registry yourself, and, I think, even the Judges are invited to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. After each hearing, we give all the parties the transcript, either in English or in French, and so according to their wishes, and they have ten days to put all the corrections they want into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. President, is not simply correcting the transcript. In the last ten minutes, we have had two answers by the witness that were not picked up at all. There was no answer in the transcript. We went back, I caught both of them. I heard the witness answer in BSC. There was no English answer picked up in the translation booth. There was nothing on the transcript to correct. So if we didn't stop in reading the transcript later, there just would be no answer, and the witness is gone at that point. So I'm concerned that, for whatever reason, the quality of the translation and/or transcription is not what we have had in this case to date. It is important that this witness's testimony, like every witness's testimony, be transcribed and translated as accurately as possible. We need, perhaps, to slow down, and I'm advising my co-counsel of that, but I would ask the Court and the registrar to inquire into this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So we have got two problems here. One is the general problem of the correction of the transcript. So for that problem, I would like to ask all of you to very carefully read the transcript in the ten-day period. We, the Judges, we also do it, and we know that everything is going to be corrected in the ten days. All the parties are invited to put all the corrections to the transcript and give it to the registry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which does not mean that a very important error may not be put forward -- pointed out straight away. That's the way we've been proceeding since the very beginning. Now we have a second problem which was raised by Mr. Hayman, which is if a reply has not been given, because otherwise the parties will not be able to correct it, which asks for a spontaneous intervention, as was just made by right now by Mr. Hayman. Thank you Mr. Hayman, or thank you Mr. Nobilo. What is the reason for it? Are we maybe speaking too quickly? Have the transcripters got problems?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're probably going too quickly, because the counsel and the witness are speaking the same language. As for the interpretation, these are the same people that have been working with us for the past year, and I think that it is also sometimes -- there is a difference because we also hear the interpretation directly into French, so there can be differences in French and in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So maybe we do not need to correct all the errors straight away, because we have ten days for it, and I know that our court reporters work very hard every evening, but if there is a major error, please correct it straight away and also please speak more slowly, but also we are going to have a pause in some ten or fifteen minutes, because we're going to work longer hours tonight. Please proceed, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Certainly we shall all do our best to make the transcript as accurate as possible, and this applies to the Defence and to the witness, so we shall do our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have before us now a document of the municipal defence staff of Kiseljak dated 5th August, 1992, D-185. So let us repeat the question. The question was: What was the purpose and intention of drafting this document? What were the aims of the BH army at that time, as can be seen from this document dated the 5th of August, 1992? Please focus on point 3 of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the purpose of this document is to prepare TO units of the BH army for carrying out combat operations, reconnaissance, observation, collection of information in the field within the territory of the municipality, control of key communication lines, and that the facilities should be determined straight away, and especially the main points on the main communication routes, as well as on the auxiliary roads for blocking and cutting the territory. So we can see from this document what the intentions of the authors were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is a document of the Territorial Defence, the precursor of the BH army from Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, did the Territorial Defence, indeed, act in accordance with this document, and did it cut the main road running through Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher's assistance for the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D186 and D186A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence has supplied the translation service with copies to be translated into both languages, and if the French translation is missing, it is not due to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, have you seen this notebook?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When, and how, and under which circumstances, and who is the owner?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The owner of this notebook is Enes Varupa who was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I know he was a commander of a unit in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Enes Varupa. Could we please look at page 4, dated 11th of April, 1998. On the right-hand side marked with the date 11 April, 1993, and this is the fourth page of the original diary. What does this list of detachments mean, well-known villages are mentioned, Bila, Grabovica, Kruscica, Vrcerska (phoen), Tolovici, Sivrno Selo, Ahmici, Gacice. What do the names of these villages signify in this context?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The names of these villages mean that units are being formed in each of these villages, units of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And the date is the 11th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This means --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just a moment. Something else, Mr. President, we have just established that the English translation has an error. In the English translation, we see the 11th of April, 1993, whereas, in the original document, it is 11th of April, 1992. So can this correction be made? I'm referring to the fourth page of the original text. So you said that this list of villages is, in fact, a list of villages in which Territorial Defence units were stationed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Will you please look at the next page, and this is page 5 of the Croatian original, and in the English translation, there is no date, but it begins Preocica squad. Perhaps it would be a good idea if the usher could switch on the ELMO and put this document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters in the booth do not have any of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could the ELMO be switched on, please? Please press the button for our witness so he can look, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please explain the text? Again, we have the names of the villages, we have some numbers next to the names of villages. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The numbers mean the number of troops, the number of soldiers, in those villages. And here we also have the unit indicated. For example, Preocica, is a company of 85, in Ljubic a platoon of 25, in Ljubic, sorry, 16. In Bukve, a platoon of 11, I think. In Bila, a company of 85, Preocica, also a company of 85. Vrhovine, a company of 85; Ahmici, a company of 85, but then the words Pirici Nadioci have been added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: A little more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: These three hamlets, the two hamlets next to Preocica are called Pirici and Nadioci, which means that within this whole region, there were 85 men or a company. Then, Tolovici the number 26; Kruscica a detachment of 200, Dubravica a platoon, he didn't have the numbers, but he said it was a platoon. Lupac a platoon of 25, Sadovaca a platoon of 25, Muratovici a platoon of 25, then Donja Veceriska a platoon of 25, Stari Vitez a detachment of 230, Vranska a company of 85, Gacice a platoon of 25, Donja Dubravica a company of 69. A total of about 1.300 men, but for Sivrino Selo, he didn't have the figures either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Judges in which municipality are those villages and who were the inhabitants of those villages?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: These villages are in Vitez municipality. In 1992, they were mostly inhabited by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next page, page 6, but the left-hand side, please? Could we ask the usher to assist us so that we can see page 6 on the ELMO? On page 6 and page 3 of the translation taken from the same diary of Enes Varupa we have a list of detachments. Can you tell us, within the system of Territorial Defence, how large were these detachments? What was their strength in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Between 200 and 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you list the detachments mentioned in Enes Varupa's notebook?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: There's the Bila detachment, and he lists the villages, Samovaca, Bukva, Divjake, Muratovici (phoen) then Vitez, the second detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The detachment of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Which includes Rijeka, Kolonija, and Stari Vitez. This is the urban area. Then Kruscica, which covers Vranska, in addition to Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The fourth detachment, what does it include?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Poculica, it includes Vrhovine, Lupac, Preocica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Then the fifth detachment?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Ahmici, Dubravica, and Sivrino Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is a notebook of one of the commanders, Enes Varupa, one of the TO commanders captured by the HVO, and you saw that notebook during the Croatian Muslim war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you changing the subject now, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No. I'm going on to another document which is rather lengthy, and if you agree, this would be a convenient moment for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have a ten-minute break then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we move on to another document, let us clear up something that we saw in the transcript. Enes Varupa, when was he captured please? What month and what year? The owner of this notebook that we've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Enes Varupa was captured at Grbavica in 1993. I cannot recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it after a battle at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Enes Varupa was not a commander in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. He was commander at Grbavica, but he is a native of Bukve.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Has he survived, or was he exchanged?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. He was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So he still is alive?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document that I would like the usher's assistance with, we have the text in Croatian and an English translation. The Croatian text has three pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D187 and D187A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you please take a close look at this document? It is apparently from Busovaca. Will you please look at it and read it? Brigadier, this document was issued by the Nikola Subic Zrinjski Brigade. That is what is stated in the heading. It is signed by assistant chief of staff of HOS, Zeljko Katava, signed. Will you please tell the Court, did you have this document in your possession during the Croatian/Muslim war, or just before it broke out in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was it addressed to you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So please correct me if I'm wrong when it says to the chief of VOS OZSBV Vitez, was that you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, and Mr. Nobilo. The transcript says "HOS." In the question he answers "yes," so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I thank my learned friend for helping me with the transcript. It is VOS, not HOS.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So I would now like to ask the witness to explain what VOS means, what the acronym stands for?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: VOS means military intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document is addressed to the command of the operative zones for Central Bosnia, but also to the chief of the military intelligence for the Central Bosnia operative zone. Was that you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document was addressed by the assistant chief of the military intelligence service, Zeljko Katava. Did you know him and is this his signature?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him, and this is his document and his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you receive this document sometime in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How would you describe such a document? What does it represent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It represents the current situation of the BH army in this period of time and an assessment on the part of Zeljko Katava regarding the intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The intentions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, the intentions of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please look at point 2, item 2, and read and explain what are the routes of which the head of the military intelligence believes could be cut? So will you please read it very slowly so that it goes down in the transcript accurately.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The routes that may be cut by the Muslim forces are as follows: Busovaca-Kiseljak, in the region of the village of Kacuni. Busovaca-Vitez in the region of the village of Ahmici and Busovaca-Zenica in the region of the village of Grablje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So that was the assessment of the military intelligence service of the Busovaca Brigade in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document is self-explanatory, especially page 1, where specific locations are indicated in Busovaca where units of the BH army were accommodated?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should like to go on to the next document, please. This is Exhibit No. D188, Mr. Registrar, in the Croatian and English versions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, 188 for the BCS and 188A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a document dated 12th of February, 1993, from the 3rd Corps of the BH army compiled by the commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. Could you tell the Court whether you saw this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When and under which circumstances?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I received this document from a source that I would not like to reveal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did this source copy this document from Hadzihasanovic's hard disc?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page there is some handwriting in black ink and somebody has initialled it. Whose handwriting is this?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It is the handwriting of Colonel Tihomir Blaskic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will read to you from the middle of the text. So could you please tell me whether this was correct that Colonel Blaskic was indeed where the document says he was. So I quote: "The document which arrived as a reply was not signed by Tiho Blaskic but by somebody for us who was not authorised by you. We assume that Colonel Tihomir Blaskic is isolated in Kiseljak and that readiness has been expressed to deal with the problem was a put-up affair and that the problems are, in fact, being resolved by somebody else and not Tihomir Blaskic, and that, therefore, there is no point in negotiating in this way because no results can be expected from such negotiations."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher in future to try and place the English version on the ELMO or the Croatian version so this will be of assistance to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you tell us, is it true that at the time of the January conflict in Busovaca, and even during February, Colonel Blaskic was in Kiseljak and he couldn't come to the area of Busovaca and Vitez? Shall I repeat the question if you were not listening? My question is -- what I have just read -- is it true that Colonel Blaskic, during the January conflict in Busovaca and later in the course of February, remained isolated in Kiseljak, and that he was unable in January and February to come to Busovaca and Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. The Colonel was in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Why does Hadzihasanovic say that Blaskic was isolated in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That was his opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Are you sure that Colonel Blaskic was in Vitez at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I think he was, but I was based in Bila, so I didn't really pay attention to whether he was in Kiseljak or Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you didn't see the Colonel at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D189, 189A for the French version and 189B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this document, which also belongs to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and which was issued on the 22nd of March, 1993, did you have it in your possession in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Who is Mustafa Hajrulahovic Talijan? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: His position at the time was commander of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, we won't comment because the text is self-explanatory. I should now like to go on to the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D190 and D190A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could the witness be given the Croatian version, please, because he doesn't read English?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please look at this document closely, leaf through it, and then we shall comment on it. Brigadier, who compiled this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This document was compiled by me or, rather, in my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was compiled on the 25th of March, 1993 as indicated?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it represent? Will you describe it yourself? What does this document, as such, represent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This document represents an assessment of the situation in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But in essence, does it represent what the title says, "Assessment of possible aggressor activities within the territories of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How was this document drawn up? What was it based on? Does it consist of facts, your analysis? Will you describe what it means amongst intelligence people when you talk of assessments?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: You take into consideration all of the relevant indicators and developments on the ground, so on the basis of all data collected, that we were able to come by in the territory of the entire Operative Zone, we made an estimate of the possible activities of the aggressor within the territory of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I ask you to turn to page 2, so we can focus on the subject of this indictment, that is, Busovaca-Travnik and Novi Travnik which is on the bottom of the page? Will you please read or comment what your estimate was on the 25th of March, 1993 as to what could happen in the municipalities of Busovaca, Vitez, Travnik and Novi Travnik. These figures on the bottom of page 2 and on page 3, so reading the note, will you please comment on your estimate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Our estimate was that the main conflict within the territory of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia would be over the places covered by this territory, that is, the territory of Busovaca, Vitez, Travnik and Novi Travnik. There were many reasons for this, and we mentioned some of them, including the fact that extremely important military industry facilities were located in this area, that is, the factory of ammunition, that in this area, there was the command of the Operative Zone for Central Bosnia, the logistics, that these areas, separate from Zenica and Visoko, the settlements of Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Bugonjo, and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And on the next page, which is most important of all?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The intentions of the potential aggressor are to place under his control this area, and to topple the HVO, and to link up with the fringe municipalities in the southern part of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, what was your estimate at the time along which axis would the BH army attack, if they did so?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was our estimate that the offensives of the BH army would be directed against the areas of Busovaca and Vitez along the axis Kacuni-Busovaca, Kaonik-Vitez, Zenica-Kuber, along the Lasva River Valley, Kaonik-Vitez, Zenica-Preocica-Vitez, and that these operations would start from the Kacuni-Kuber areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us leave out Novi Travnik and Travnik that is referred to in this document, but we would like to focus on your conclusions in the last two paragraphs, beginning with following and analysing the activities of the potential aggressor so far. They apply the aggressor tactics. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It means that the BH army fully applied the same tactics as the army of Bosnian Serbs or, that is, the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say the tactics of the army of Republika Srpska, is that what you said; that by its activities, the BH army would capture each part of the territory, regulate positions, move out the Croatian inhabitants, and take full control. So that was the tactics of the army of Republika Srpska that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In view of the time distance that has passed, that is, it is more than five years since that date in 1993, was your assessment at the time -- has it been proven to be correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you submit that estimate to Colonel Blaskic on the 25th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher's assistance for the next exhibit? Is this your signature? Did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. This was signed by my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D191, and D191A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, have you got the Croatian text?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this is document D191. Did you see this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This is a document that comes from a meeting from several brigades of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the police of the ministry of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could you tell the Court in which way did you come into possession of these documents of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I came into possession of this document through a man whose identity I would not like to reveal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That person brought it to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will just read the introduction. We are not going to go through the document. I'm just going to ask you one or two questions. The heading says that it comes from the minutes on the 20th of March, 1993, from the joint meeting of the representatives of the commands of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the brigades ^ Delic, Neretva, BDP 4th Corps of the Municipal Staff of Jablanica, as well as representatives of the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You saw this document also in 1993. While reading this document, what could you conclude?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: When we were reading this document, we concluded that an attack would happen and also military operations towards Jablanica, Konjic, and Kresevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That means that these minutes are an agreement for military operation, but against whom?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And after that meeting, did it occur?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us proceed. Please, could you show the next document now? This document exists in three languages, in Croatian, in French, and in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D192, 192A for the French version, and 192B for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If we take a look at this document, we can see that it was issued by the command of the Vitez Brigade on the 10th of April, 1993, so six days before the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims in the Vitez municipality. And it was compiled, again, by the VOS, that is, the military intelligence service, and precisely, Tomislav Krizanac. First of all, this document D192 as it was marked here, did you see this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to its contents, were the contents or the whole document, indeed, forwarded to the Commander Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. It was through the assessment of my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In this document, it says that the 325th Mountain Brigade deploys four battalions and that these battalions are deployed in various villages, Pirici, Ahmici, Santici, Tolovici, Sivrino Selo, Kruscica, Gacice, Donja Vecerisko, and so on and so forth. Let us not numerate all the villages. Those villages that are stated here as places where parts of the 325th Brigades are deployed, are all these villages in the Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: These are the estimates made by Mr. Tomislav Krizanac. As his superior, were you completely -- did you completely approve of his assessment or were some mistakes made?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I think that there were some mistakes concerning the battalion in Bukve.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So he made a slight mistake in his estimates?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As for the rest, did Tomislav Krizanac give correct estimates?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the document speaks for itself, so we're not going to continue reading it. Please, I would like to show the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D193, 193A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, this document comes from the Brigade Nikola Subic Zrinkjski from Busovaca, and it was obviously compiled by the deputy chief of VOS, that is, the military intelligence service, Zeljko Katava. Did you see this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document was compiled on the 14th of April, 1993, that is, two days before the conflict broke out in the Lasva River Valley in the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca. In the English translation it says the 14th of March, 1993, and the Croatian text says that number 3 was corrected into number 4, so there was a mistake. Can you please help us, Brigadier, was this text written in March or April 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It comes from the 14th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So this was wrongly typed. Could you please take a close look? Does it say the 14th of April, after all, because the text says during the mobilisation in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. It was April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it means that it was written March -- so number 3, and somebody found a mistake and crossed it out and wrote 4. So can we be 100 per cent sure that it was in April, because it speaks about the general mobilisation in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is the 14th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In that case I'm right when I say that it was two days before the break-out of the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This report starts in the following way: During the proclamation of general mobilisation in Zenica, we estimate that the following might happen. Brigadier, do I understand this correctly when I say that the military intelligence service, once it had found out that already on the 14th in Zenica, a general mobilisation was declared, that it made a correct estimate of what the BH army wanted to do, that is, where it wanted to attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me now read to you the first part of it, where it says: "The military intelligence service, the next offensive action could be made out of two parts." I'm going to read it now to see in what way this estimate was correct. So about the offensive action of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And now I quote: "The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina could maybe try and attempt with a skillful manoeuvre to avoid the control of the HVO Cajdras by going through the territory under its control and that is Zenica-Vrazale-Dobriljeno (756) Vrhovine, and then an attack on Ahmici (because of the cutting off of Busovaca and Vitez) and then joining via Rovna with Vranjska." In the second part it speaks about activities in Novi Travnik. Could you please tell me, due to facts from this estimate, did they land on the table of the office of Mr. Blaskic on the 14th of April, 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This report first came to the department. It was status and then either as a report or as an estimate, it was forwarded to the command of the operational zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know in what way Colonel Blaskic worked? Was it possible that extremely important reports arrived at his office and that he would not have a look at them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. That would not be possible. It was not possible that an important report would come to his office and that he does not read it. He was taking note of everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether the attack towards Vrhovine went from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So it really did happen?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask you for some assistance now, please? The next document is also in Croatian and in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D194 and D194A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina which the Defence has received, kindly, from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and after an order issued by this Trial Chamber. This document comes from the 303rd Glorious Brigade from Zenica on the 16th of April, 1994, at midday. That was the day when the war broke out between the Croats and the Muslims in the municipalities of Vitez and Busovaca. I would like to draw the attention of the witness to paragraph 4, towards the end of the first page of the Croatian text in paragraph 4 where the commander says: "I have decided."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will now read and quote, and after that, please listen carefully, I will ask you questions about it. "In order to carry out the order of the 3rd Corps command" -- and now we have the numbers, which means confidential, "number 02/33" -- then it cannot be read. I draw your attention to the 15th of April, 1993. So the basis of this order is the order of the command of the 3rd Corps from the previous day, the day before the conflict broke out, to the units of the brigade to make the movement in the route "Zenica-Drivusa-Janjici," or something like that. It's not very legible. "Janjicki vrh-Gumanci, with the assignment of occupying a defensive area along the following line: Saracevica structure (trig point 957) Kicin (trig point 921)," and then, Trebinje (trig point 567), where, after consolidating the defence, an attack has to be made along the main communication route, Saracevica, Jelinak, Loncari, with the task to take control in the facilities Obla Glava, and then have an infantry attack along the lines Saracevica, Vrela, and to come to the trig point 393, Vrana Stijena, Bakije, Katici, and then be ready to continue towards the communication Vitez, Busovaca." Colleague Hayman has informed me that in the English text the date is wrong, the date of the command in the English text. When we see the Croatian text, it is very -- we can easily see it was the 15th of April, 1993, and not the 4th of April. So it was translated in this Tribunal, but nevertheless, a mistake was made. So, please, could you focus on the ELMO at that particular line so that we can see the date. So the command issued by the 3rd Corps, the commander speaks of the attack. This command of the 3rd Corps was issued on the 15th of April. You can see where the pointer is. Brigadier, this is the command of the 33rd Glorious Brigade from Zenica. This is its official name, which makes reference to a confidential command of the 3rd Corps from Zenica of the 15th of April. What does this document say to you? You haven't seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This document says that the command was given to just one unit. In this case, everybody received the command, but the 303rd Brigade had to make an attack going from Zenica towards Busovaca. So its objective was to come to the communication line of Vitez-Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So the 303rd Brigade, on the 16th of April at midday, is issuing to its units such a command, and the 3rd Corps, the day earlier on the 15th of April? Did you know of it before?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But you had estimates that went along those lines?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. We had the information, but we had it much earlier. Somewhere around the 10th, we heard that preparations were made in order to carry out military operations in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you please stand up, take this piece of paper, and show these lines, according to what the text says? Could you please show it on this map, and then tell us whether it was really carried out in such a way.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is Zenica, the command of the 3rd Corps --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you please show to the Court the direction going from Zenica towards Loncari?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: So it goes from Zenica, Grevisa (phoen), which was not drawn here, then Janjicki, and this direction here towards Loncari, and then going around Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The question now is: Did the attack happen in that way, the attack on the municipality of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: One of the attacks was as described. There were various lines of attack. One came also from the village of Lasva and Dusina, and one of the lines of the attack was this one, and this was the main line of attack (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could we please have the next document now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D195 and D195A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, just to speed things up, I will read now the key sentences that are most relevant for the Defence, and I would like to ask you to comment. First of all, have you seen this document? Did you see it in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The title here is the 22nd of April, 1992. Is this a mistake when it comes to the contents of the text?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. It is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. There are quite often such mistakes. So what it says "VOS," that is, the military intelligence service of the Vitez Brigade, and it says: "The command of the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia to the Military Information Service." That is your department. I quote and I'm reading from the second paragraph: "In the evening, a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was captured and an investigation was started." I'm now going to skip a paragraph, where he gave some intelligence information about the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and pass on to the relevant fourth paragraph. "We can see that in the region - Mahala, there are, all in all, some 300 members or soldiers very well-armed. Apart from light infantry weapons, they have got a large quantity of PMK-53 PAT IMB," and later on, I will ask you to explain what that means, "with some 60 boxes of shells," and there is also a mark which we'll explain after that. "The deployment of personnel, the trenches, and the shelters have been made around every Muslim house. The strongest points are in Mahala Rakite near the cooperative building, the shop of Metal Borac near the cemetary, Donja Mahala, etc." About more detailed deployment, "We will forward the report on the following day according to the tables of deployment which is being compiled." So this is the information given by a prisoner of war, where you got the information that there were 350 soldiers with light infantry weapons and some heavier weapons. Could you please tell us what are these military abbreviations, "PMK-53"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is a machine gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it mean, "PAT"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: "PAT" means anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It can be used also during fighting on the ground?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does it mean, "MB"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That means mortar with some 60 boxes of shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How many shells are there in each box?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Six, six shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So in every box, there are six shells, and they had 60 boxes. Also, they speak of something called "RB," hand-held launcher of 40 millimetres. Therefore, this document that you obtained from the military intelligence of the Viteska Brigade on the 22nd of April, 1993, did you familiarise Commander Blaskic with this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Accompanying our regular reports or through our estimates, General Blaskic was informed about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, that ends our examination-in-chief, and we should like to tender the exhibits that we used today, from D184, 185, 186, to D193, as Defence Exhibits. I beg your pardon. 195, the last number is 195. Therefore, from D184 to D195.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objections? Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could just review my notes for one minute, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: As the examination-in-chief is over, perhaps this is a good time to have a break, and we will resume at 5.00, which will give the Prosecutor a chance to review his notes and express his views when we resume. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo, you wanted to tender the documents; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. And in addition to what I have tendered, I should also like to tender the maps which were shown on the screen, maps 1 to 15. I think they are on the table now. Could all these maps be given a single number slash 1 through 15 for each of the maps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 283/1 (sic) through to /15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before beginning your cross-examination, I asked Mr. Harmon whether he had any comments regarding D183/1 through /15 and then D184 to 195. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no objection to any of the exhibits, with one exception. That is, I have an inquiry with respect to D186, because D186 appears, at least at first blush to the Prosecutor's office, to be a portion of the notebook and not the complete notebook. The question I have and I would ask of Mr. Nobilo, is this what has been presented as D186, a copy of the complete notebook that was seized, or are there other portions that have not been reproduced?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is a copy of the whole notebook, but we have translated into English only three pages which we consider to be relevant, but in the Croatian version, there's a copy of the whole notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then I have no objection to 186, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. In that case, all of these documents have been admitted into evidence. It is now up to you, Mr. Harmon, to continue with the cross-examination, or someone else?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will conduct the cross-examination of Brigadier Zeko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Brigadier Zeko.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You testified in your direct examination that you are a career military officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What year did you graduate from the military academy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When did you go to Slovenia to serve your duty in that particular republic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you remain there until you left for Germany in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You served, did you not, in the Postanje garrison in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that the same garrison where Colonel Blaskic served?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you know Colonel Blaskic when you were serving in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you friends with Colonel Blaskic when you were serving with him in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you know him while you were serving in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In what capacity did you know him, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I know that he was the commander of a unit, and I was a commander of a reconnaissance company which was under the direct command of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you under his command, or were you under the command of somebody else while you were serving in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I was under somebody else's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was Colonel Blaskic the assistant commander, or a deputy commander, of a motorised battalion while he was in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know what his duties were while he was in Slovenia, Brigadier Zeko?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I know that he was a commander of a company in a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was he also the assistant commander for political affairs?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you were called by the Defence Department in Novi Travnik in February of 1992. Who called you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Zoran Matosovic from the Defence Department of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
